vocabulary.meaning: mental or emotional pressure caused by work conditions or demands
examples: Workplace stress is an important idea when discussing stress in the workplace.
Learning about workplace stress can help us understand this issue more clearly.

vocabulary.meaning: a fixed time by which a task must be completed
examples: People often have different views about deadline when discussing stress in the workplace.
Understanding deadline can make a conversation about this topic more precise.

vocabulary.meaning: the amount of work a person is expected to do
examples: The topic of stress in the workplace raises useful questions about workload.
We can discuss how workload affects people, communities, or the environment.

vocabulary.meaning: physical and emotional exhaustion caused by prolonged stress or overwork
examples: Burnout can play an important role in debates about stress in the workplace.
Different countries may deal with burnout in different ways.

vocabulary.meaning: a feeling of stress caused by difficult demands or expectations
examples: A discussion about stress in the workplace can include the effects of pressure.
Knowing the meaning of pressure makes it easier to express an opinion on this issue.

vocabulary.meaning: a healthy balance between work responsibilities and personal life
examples: Work-life balance is useful vocabulary for talking about stress in the workplace.
We can use the idea of work-life balance to compare different experiences and viewpoints.
